definitions.explanation: A very large number of people, animals, or things gathered or moving together.

examples.japanese: イワシの{大群|たいぐん}が{現|あらわ}れた。
examples.english: A huge school of sardines appeared.

examples.japanese: バッタの{大群|たいぐん}が{農地|のうち}を{襲|おそ}った。
examples.english: A swarm of locusts attacked the farmland.

examples.japanese: {観光|かんこう}シーズンになると、{大群|たいぐん}の{観光客|かんこうきゃく}がこの{島|しま}を{訪|おとず}れる。
examples.english: When tourist season arrives, throngs of tourists visit this island.

notes:
Composed of {大|たい} (large) + {群|ぐん} (group, flock). Used for impressively large numbers of living things — animals, insects, people — or sometimes objects. The word emphasizes the sheer scale of the group.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蝶|ちょう}の{大群|たいぐん}: a swarm of butterflies
- {大群|たいぐん}で{押|お}し{寄|よ}せる: to swarm in; to descend in large numbers
- {大群|たいぐん}が{発生|はっせい}する: a large group/swarm appears

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {群|む}れ: group; flock; herd — more neutral in size
- {集団|しゅうだん}: group; mass — more organized, often used for people
- {群衆|ぐんしゅう}: crowd; throng — specifically a crowd of people
